chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan al-Sayqal, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, immorality, obscenity, and insolence are from hypocrisy.'

key_terms.الْفُحْش: Immorality or coarseness in speech and action

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of hypocrisy in behavior according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies foul speech, obscenity, and insolance as intrinsic markers of hypocrisy (nifaq), linking outward behavioral traits directly to inner spiritual deficiency. In Shia scholarly tradition, this hadith is often cited to demonstrate that moral decay in communication reflects a corruption of the heart, serving as a diagnostic tool for assessing the depth of one's faith beyond mere ritual observance.
